chunks: Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja'far عليه السلام, who said:

Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام gave judgment concerning a man for whom he had ordered that his right hand be cut off, but his left hand was presented, so they cut it off, thinking it was his right. Then they said, “We only cut off his left hand.” Should his right hand be cut off? He said: “His right hand is not to be cut off, while his left has already been cut off.”
And he said concerning a man who took a helmet from the war booty, and they said, “He has stolen, so cut him off,” that: “I do not cut anyone in respect of what he took while he had a share in it.”

key_terms.أَمِيرُ ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Amir al-Mu'minin, Imam Ali عليه السلام, the authority issuing the legal judgment
key_terms.بَيْضَةً: a helmet taken from the spoils
key_terms.سَرَقَ: he stole; the accusation of theft made against the man
key_terms.شِرْكٌ: a share or joint entitlement in the property taken
key_terms.شِمَالُهُ: his left hand, the limb mistakenly cut instead of the right
key_terms.يَمِينُهُ: his right hand, the prescribed limb in the theft punishment
key_terms.ٱلْمَغْنَمِ: war booty or spoils in which eligible participants have a share

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if the wrong hand is cut in a theft punishment, and is the hadd applied for taking from shared war booty?
ai.summary: This hadith transmits legal rulings from Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام on theft-related punishments. It states that if the wrong hand was cut in place of the prescribed right hand, the right hand is not then cut, and that the hadd of theft is not applied to one who takes from war booty in which he already has a share.
